paragraph_audit.reason: License title, version, date, and URL identify the document but impose no activity constraint.
Terms-and-conditions heading; it supplies context but creates no operative rule.
Definitions heading only.
Defines License by reference to §§1–9; contextual cross-reference, not a standalone grant or duty.
Defines Licensor; used to interpret grantors and recipients but imposes no standalone rule.
Defines Legal Entity and control; used to interpret the licensee definition but is not itself an operative rule.
Defines You/Your as the person or entity exercising permissions; contextual actor definition.
Defines Source form; contextual form distinction used in operative provisions.
Defines Object form; contextual form distinction used in operative provisions.
Defines Work and how it is identified; contextual scope definition.
Defines Derivative Works and excludes separable works and mere linking/binding to interfaces; contextual scope boundary.
Defines Contribution, including the meaning of intentional submission and the Not a Contribution exception; contextual definition for later provisions.
Defines Contributor; contextual identification of grantors.
Section 2 grants reproduction, preparation of Derivative Works, sublicensing, and distribution rights; distribution clauses capture the linked §4 conditions.
Section 3's limited patent grant and patent-litigation termination consequence are represented; unavailable distinct patent activities are disclosed in coverage notes.
Section 4's redistribution permission applies in any medium, with or without modifications, and in Source or Object form; recipient License-copy condition is represented.
Section 4(a) requires a License copy for recipients of the Work or Derivative Works.
Section 4(b) requires prominent change notices when modified files are distributed.
Section 4(c) notice-retention duty and its distributed-Derivative-Work Source-form and pertinence limits are represented.
Section 4(d) NOTICE-file prerequisite, derivative-distribution trigger, pertinence limit, alternative placement options, and limits on added attribution notices are represented.
Section 4 permits copyright statements and additional or different terms for modifications or a Derivative Work as a whole, conditioned on otherwise complying with the License.

The default terms for intentionally submitted Contributions, explicit-statement exception, and separate-agreement carveout are captured, but submission has no precise matching canonical activity/object; the clause uses an imperfect representation.
Section 6 withholds general permission to use Licensor names and marks while specifying the reasonable-and-customary origin-description and NOTICE-reproduction exception.
Warranty and condition disclaimers and allocation of responsibility for assessing use and redistribution; no behavioral duty governing a licensed activity is extracted under the task rules.
Limitation of Contributor liability; excluded as nonoperative warranty/liability boilerplate.
Section 9 gives a conditional permission to offer and charge for specified additional obligations or rights during redistribution, subject to own-behalf and indemnity duties.
End-of-terms marker; no operative rule.
Appendix heading introducing application instructions; not an operative license rule.
Instructions for applying the Apache License notice to one's work, including recommendations about identification; not an operative license duty for this extraction.
Copyright notice template with symbolic fields; not an operative rule.
Appendix boilerplate notice and location for obtaining the License; instructional/template text, not an additional operative rule.
URL supplied as part of the appendix instructions; no operative activity constraint.
Warranty disclaimer and direction to consult the License text, included as appendix boilerplate rather than an operative activity rule.

coverage_notes.note: The license text identifies Apache License 2.0. The Appendix mentioned in the definition of Work is not supplied; its example is not needed to interpret the extracted rules.
Section 2 also grants public display and public performance permissions, for which no matching canonical activity is available.

Section 3 expressly grants make, have made, import, and use rights; the available activity vocabulary cannot distinctly represent all of those actions. Patent grant scope and termination are stated in the clause explanations.
Section 5 concerns submission of a Contribution; no precise activity/object pair is available, so its clause uses an imperfect activity representation and the audit marks it unresolved.
The supplied excerpt is the Apache License 2.0 ending and appendix. The extracted permission in section 9 is conditional on its stated redistribution and acceptance circumstances.

The warranty disclaimer and limitation of liability are excluded as nonoperative for this activity-constraint extraction. The appendix contains application instructions and boilerplate/example notice text, not additional operative license permissions or duties.
